findings.F1: On the Sunday bar, a coin's 1-day move reverses over the next 3 days, and it reverses most when weekend volume was thin. Over all Sundays the slope of the standardised excess 3-day return on the Sunday z-score is −0.085 (t −3.76, 4041 cases; t −1.75 when the coins are averaged per date over 338 dates). On Sundays whose two-day weekend volume is below the coin's median, the date-clustered t is −2.36 over 298 dates, against −1.37 over 316 dates for the high-volume half.
findings.F2: In the thin-volume Sundays the reversal is graded across the whole range of the move and covers rises as well as falls. By Sunday z-quintile, the excess 3-day return runs +1.36 %, +1.27 %, −0.41 %, −1.26 % and −1.12 % (about 398 cases each). In a regression over all Sundays, the term z × log(weekend volume ratio) is +0.065 (t 1.93): the thinner the weekend, the stronger the reversal.
findings.F3: The thin-weekend reversal is broad across coins and years. Its slope is negative in 15 of 19 coins (79 %; in LINK t −3.93, AAVE −2.94, NEAR −2.37, ETH −2.17). It is negative in 7 of 8 years, with 2022 the exception (+0.018, t 0.12). No single year is significant on its own (|t| at most 1.29).
findings.F4: On weekdays there is no such reversal. On Monday-to-Thursday bars the slope on z is +0.008 (t 0.68), and its interaction with volume is +0.022 (t 1.57). The slope on z is negative only on Sunday; Wednesday, Friday and Saturday show positive slopes (t 2.86, 3.79, 3.26 unclustered).
findings.F5: The tested idea's volatility leg is not supported: Sunday falls rebound no more when recent volatility is high. Within Sunday falls, the slope is −0.35 (t −2.82) in the calmest volatility tercile and −0.24 (t −1.74) in the most agitated, with 271–272 cases each. Over all bars, weekend slopes are −0.02, −0.08 and −0.03 across calm, mid and agitated terciles.
findings.F6: Friday moves tend to continue over the next 3 days, but this does not stand out once dependence is counted. The Friday z-quintile excess returns run −1.21 %, +0.32 %, +0.22 %, +0.62 % and +0.71 % (about 802 each), and 74 % of coins have a positive slope. But the date-clustered t is only 1.36, and the yearly slope flips sign (2024 t +5.64, 2025 t −2.98).
findings.F7: The book's risk sits entirely in the Monday-to-Wednesday holding days. Their daily standard deviation is 1.43–1.70 %, against 0.21–0.31 % on the other days. Those three days hold 380 of the 1 % worst coin-days and 340 of the 1 % best. The deepest falls are window-specific: w3 −16.8 % (sum −10.1 %) and w2 −14.5 %, which is what holds the Calmar at 0.37.

ideas.idea: A coin's Sunday close-to-close move, a fall or a rise, is partly undone over the next 3 days, and the thinner the weekend's volume against the coin's usual 20-day volume, the larger the share of the move that is undone.
ideas.consequence: A trader would fade a Sunday move into the start of the week, leaning harder the thinner the weekend's volume was, and would refuse to fade Sunday moves made on heavy volume.
ideas.name: thin-weekend Sunday move reverses
